## Competitive Brief: Zonoid vs Full Landscape (June 2026)

### 1. One-line positioning

The only system where every completed task makes future tasks cheaper, smarter, and verifiably better.

---

### 2. Market gap in one paragraph

Across 200+ tools surveyed — orchestration frameworks, AI coding agents, and task/workflow platforms — every competitor treats memory and execution as separate concerns. Frameworks (LangGraph, Temporal, Dagster) durable-ify execution but leave knowledge extraction as a manual afterthought. Coding agents (claude-mem, Devin, Cline) capture tool-call results in flat timelines but have no task graph, no quality signal, no budget tracking, and no closed improvement loop. Task tools (Asana, Linear, Beads) model work graphs but treat AI output as an opaque black box that leaves no structured residue. The gap is the same in every category: nobody closes the loop from "work was done" to "system got smarter in a measurable, reproducible way." Zonoid occupies that gap — execution and memory are the same data structure, every task outcome is receipted (cost, output, quality score), and future tasks inherit exactly the right context under a token budget through a self-learning loop that measures, judges, and improves automatically.

---

### 3. Competitive moat

- Execution-memory unification: The work graph IS the memory graph. Knowledge nodes attach directly to completed task nodes with provenance edges — no separate vector store to sync, no manual extraction step, no stale snapshot problem. Competitors cannot replicate this without a ground-up redesign of their data model.
- Receipted outcomes as a primitive: Every task records what it cost in tokens, what it produced, and what quality score the judge assigned. This enables autonomy-drift tracking and ROI calculation that no competitor — open-source or enterprise — ships as a native observable.
